record.paper_title: 二分決定グラフに基づく計算複雑さに関する未解決問題について
record.context_brief: one-way NL versus one-way parity logspace
record.original_question: Let l-NL be one-way-input nondeterministic logarithmic-space computation, and let l-⊕L be one-way-input logarithmic-space nondeterministic computation with parity acceptance, where an input is accepted when an odd number of computation paths reach an accepting state. Does the nonuniform inclusion NL ⊆ ⊕L carry over to the one-way-input setting, that is, can one prove l-NL ⊆ l-⊕L?

evidence.quote: 受理条件を「奇数個の計算パスで受理状態へ到達すれば受理」とした場合に、対数領域限定で計算できる関数のクラスを ⊕L と書く。
これをそのままオンライン計算モデルに持ってくることができるだろうか。即ち、l-NL⊆l-⊕L が言えるだろうか。

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Turing machines with a read-only input tape and a separate work tape of size O(log n) on inputs of length n. Call such a machine one-way-input if its input head can only move left-to-right (it never moves leftwards along the input tape).

Define the following nonuniform complexity classes:
- NL: the class of languages decided by nondeterministic logarithmic-space Turing machines (with standard two-way input access), where a string is accepted iff at least one computation path reaches an accepting state.
- ⊕L: the class of languages decided by nondeterministic logarithmic-space Turing machines under parity acceptance, where a string is accepted iff an odd number of computation paths reach an accepting state.
- l-NL: the one-way-input analogue of NL, i.e., languages decided by one-way-input nondeterministic logarithmic-space machines under existential acceptance.
- l-⊕L: the one-way-input analogue of ⊕L, i.e., languages decided by one-way-input nondeterministic logarithmic-space machines under parity acceptance.

It is known (in the nonuniform setting) that NL ⊆ ⊕L. The question is: does the analogous inclusion hold in the one-way-input model? Specifically, prove or disprove the inclusion
        l-NL ⊆ l-⊕L.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of the one-way-input inclusion l-NL ⊆ l-⊕L was located in available sources. The standard nonuniform inclusion NL ⊆ ⊕L (via Wigderson's result) is well known, but its transfer to the one-way-input (online) logspace setting does not appear to have been established or refuted in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: NL ⊆ ⊕L/poly (Wigderson)
status_evidence.snippet: Wigderson proved NL/poly ⊆ ⊕L/poly via isolation, giving the standard nonuniform inclusion of NL inside parity-L.
status_evidence.claim: The two-way (standard) inclusion NL ⊆ ⊕L in the nonuniform setting is established; the one-way-input analogue is not addressed.
